nodes.name: Critical Analysis and Reasoning Skills
nodes.description: MCAT CARS: comprehension and reasoning on humanities and social-science passages. No outside content knowledge required.

nodes.name: Foundations of Comprehension
nodes.description: Understanding the basic components of the text.

nodes.name: Main idea and primary purpose
nodes.description: Identify the author's central claim or purpose.

nodes.name: Inferring meaning
nodes.description: Draw inferences licensed by the passage.

nodes.name: Vocabulary in context
nodes.description: Determine word or phrase meaning from usage.

nodes.name: Reasoning Within the Text
nodes.description: Integrating, analyzing, and evaluating passage arguments.

nodes.name: Integration of parts
nodes.description: Relate claims, evidence, and examples across paragraphs.

nodes.name: Relevance and support
nodes.description: Judge which statements support or undermine a claim.

nodes.name: Logic and structure
nodes.description: Identify assumptions, conclusions, and argumentative moves.

nodes.name: Evaluation of tone and rhetoric
nodes.description: Assess stance, emphasis, and rhetorical strategy.

nodes.name: Internal consistency
nodes.description: Detect tensions or qualifications inside the passage.

nodes.name: Reasoning Beyond the Text
nodes.description: Applying or extrapolating ideas to new information.

nodes.name: Apply to a new context
nodes.description: Use a passage principle in an unfamiliar scenario.

nodes.name: Incorporate new information
nodes.description: Assess how extra-textual facts would affect the argument.

nodes.name: Analogies and hypotheticals
nodes.description: Map passage relationships onto analogous cases.

nodes.name: Limitations and implications
nodes.description: Extrapolate consequences the author does not state.

nodes.name: Scientific Inquiry and Reasoning Skills
nodes.description: Overlay skills on every natural and social science item. exam_weight 0 — selection uses skill_tag, not new-item quota.

Understanding
nodes.description: Close reading of humanities and social-science stimuli.

nodes.description: Identify what a humanities passage is saying.

nodes.description: Track who is speaking and how the piece is built.

nodes.name: Inference
nodes.description: Implied meaning licensed by the stimulus.

nodes.name: Unstated assumptions
nodes.description: What must be true for the speaker's position.

nodes.name: Reading between the lines in poetry

nodes.description: Detect turns inside a short extract.

nodes.name: Argument structure
nodes.description: Claims, reasons, and flaws in discursive prose.

nodes.description: Which statement better captures a dispute.

nodes.description: ACER S2; 25% of overall. Two tasks.

nodes.name: Task A — socio-cultural
nodes.description: Argumentative response to socio-cultural quote sets.

nodes.name: Written communication craft
